## Project Overview
Grounded review and UI/data work on TreeApp at `d:/5eliment/app/treeapp` (Five Elements). React Native / Expo field app: photograph trees, lock GPS, record measurements, sync to Supabase for the CARM admin panel. README still describes an early photo-and-form app; the code is a project-based survey, audit, task, and land-boundary system. Domain model is mainly `src/types/index.ts` plus Supabase migrations. Terminal is cmd.exe, not PowerShell. Python `-c` and pip do run. No successful Metro cache clear or Expo start is proven. No EAS build has produced or downloaded an APK. No local `:app:assembleRelease` has printed `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` / `BUILD FAILED`, an exit code paired with a Gradle log, or a package-task line. No markdown file has been read, and no `file_write_result` or diff has confirmed markdown contents. No script file under `scripts/` has been confirmed deleted. `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG` is visible and open and has not been read.

Latest environment is 10/5/2026, 6:20:30 PM (Asia/Calcutta, UTC+5:30). Context 120,066 tokens (60%), up from 119,428 (60%) at 6:15:09 and 6:11:57 PM, and from 105,535 (53%) at 6:09:37 PM. Earlier: 109,248 (55%) at 6:08:15; 109,630 (55%) at 6:06:02; 106,890 (53%) at 6:04:20; 101,429 (51%) at 6:02:28; 90,465 (45%) at 5:59:09; 90,785 (45%) at 5:56:05; 86,158 (43%) at 5:54:48; 85,979 (43%) at 5:48:57; 83,200 (42%) at 5:43:02; 77,312 (39%) at 5:37:00; 73,147 (37%) at 5:32:45; 92,076 (46%) at 2:27:15; 170,391 (85%) at 2:25:18; 150,015 (75%) at 12:22:33. A context-size change is an environment number only and does not erase earlier confirmed reads. The 6:20 rise adds the return of the 6:15 `supabase` `*.sql` search (“Found 11 results,” migration hit windows only) and two “did not use a tool” automations. It does not retract the 6:11 History `TreeDetailScreen.tsx` read of lines 250–319, the 6:09 types read (lines 90–159), the 6:08 unpaired “Found 8 results” (migration hit windows only; distinct from this 11-result return), the 6:08 interrupted unreturned TaskScreen read (offset 680, limit 120), the 6:06 treeStore read (lines 1–27), the 6:06 unreturned TaskScreen read (offset 90, limit 50), the 6:04 unpaired “Found 0 results,” the 6:02 treeService.ts lines 680–796 read, the 5:59 read of lines 310–449, the 2:25:58 read of lines 1057–1091, the 2:25:18 or 2:27:15 no-diff writes, or any earlier unreturned search/read. Cost $0.00. Mode Coding, model grok-4.7-max.

Visible file at 6:20:30 is `.git\COMMIT_EDITMSG` (not a read). Open tabs: `src/components/TreeCard.tsx` and `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`. TreeCard remains a tab and has no confirmed read. Previously, at 6:11:57 and 6:15:09, the visible file was `src\components\TreeCard.tsx` and it was the only open tab (same as 6:09, 6:08, 6:06, 6:04, and 6:02). The 6:06 read does not fill the 5:59 `postgres_changes|setTrees\(|addTree\(` search. The 6:08 search is not a TaskScreen or treeService read and is not the 6:20 11-result return. The 6:09 types read is not a search and not TreeDetailScreen. The 6:11 TreeDetailScreen read is not types, not treeStore, not treeService, and not the SQL search.

The 6:15 `search_files` of `supabase` (regex `INSERT INTO|tree_id|CREATE TRIGGER|tasks`, file pattern `*.sql`) NOW HAS a result: “Found 11 results,” all groups in `supabase/migrations/001_add_tree_columns.sql`. The result header does not restate the regex; the pattern is the one issued at 6:15. It does not fill the 6:08 or 6:06 TaskScreen reads, any TreeDetailScreen window, the 6:09 types read, or the 6:08 eight-window search. Returned and distinct: 5:54 HistoryScreen 340–419; 2:27:15 no-diff `file_write_result` for the 2:25:58 TreeDetailScreen edit; 5:59 treeService 310–449; 6:02 treeService printed 680–796; 6:06 treeStore 1–27; 6:08 SQL eight hit windows; 6:09 types 90–159; 6:11 TreeDetailScreen 250–319; 6:20 SQL eleven hit windows. Lines 680–796 of treeService are not line 469, not 310–449, not offset 1, and not TaskScreen 680–799. The 22-result search returned before 5:37 does not fill the 5:32:45 taskService search (`taskService.ts` is not among the 22 groups). The 5:43 “Found 1 result” prints treeService 469–471 only. The 5:48 “Found 12 results” and the 5:54 “Found 6 results” do not print `taskService.ts` or a `fetchTreeById` body. None of the later reads or the 6:20 SQL search fill those unreturned items.

APK facts that still bind: 6:11 PM prose claimed a release APK and `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` (prose only: `115,304,619` bytes, `6:10 PM`, debug keystore, `22m 47s`). 6:16:39 PM `explorer /select` of that path returned exit code 1, empty output — not a listing, size, timestamp, signature, or Gradle log. 6:35:56 PM an unnamed command (exit 0) listed `d:\5eliment\app\treeapp\android\app\build\outputs\apk\release`: one file `app-release.apk`, `10/03/2026 06:33 PM`, `115,284,635` bytes, `1 File(s)`, `0 Dir(s)`, `178,861,260,800` bytes free, volume “New Volume” serial `B4AF-D7A3`. That listing confirms printed name, size, and timestamp only. Not a Gradle log, not a signature, and not the 6:11 figures. Later environments do not repeat the listing. `gradle-release-log.txt` is named in the 11:08 list and the 6:15 reprint and is still unread. Omission does not retract the 6:35 listing and does not prove the APK is gone.

Confirmed `tsc` invocations: (1) 11:44:10 and (2) 12:18:14, both `npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false` in `d:/5eliment/app/treeapp`, timeout 120, exit 0, empty stdout. Two separate invocations. Neither quotes files, reveals a hunk, retracts the 11:40:19 or 11:35:06 save-time citations, or proves the 12:16:25 TaskScreen intended body or any TreeDetailScreen intended body landed. There is no third tsc. No tsc at 12:20:55 through 6:20:30. The 12:14:38 and 12:20:55 sentences “The typecheck passed” are intent only. Batches from 2:25 through 6:20 have no typecheck claim and no tsc invocation.

## Key Technical Decisions
Proof rules that still bind: an interrupted `attempt_completion` is not a hunk and is not acceptance. The 10/5, 11:48:14, 12:06:23, 12:07:48, 12:14:38, and 12:20:55 `attempt_completion`s were each interrupted; each result text is intent only and each tool use is unsuccessful. There is no `attempt_completion` from 12:09:16 through 6:20:30. A returned completion that only carries user feedback is not acceptance. A line citation inside an interrupted or unreturned completion is not a read. An issued tool call without a result is not a confirmed write, read, search, command, or todo change. An interrupted tool call confirms only that no result was returned. An IDE notice without a diff is not a hunk. A “Recently Modified Files” / “file was just edited” line is not a hunk, not a read, and not a `file_write_result`. A `file_write_result` that says `modified` but shows no diff confirms modification of that path only. A notice that changes were seen, or to treat them as the new baseline, does not supply a hunk and does not prove which bytes changed. A later such result for the same path does not show whether the bytes differ from an earlier one. TypeScript problems printed inside a `file_write_result` confirm those quoted lines and that diagnostic only. Absence of compiler problems is not proof the file typechecks and not proof any symbol was removed. A later `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 with empty stdout confirms only that invocation’s reported success and no captured stdout. A prose claim that typecheck passed is not an invocation. A confirmed read of one slice does not prove text outside that slice. A later read supersedes earlier hits for those same lines only. A later search does not erase an earlier confirmed read of lines it does not reprint. Search hits outside a later read are not reconfirmed, and their line numbers are unreliable if earlier lines in that file are now known to differ. A search-result header that does not restate the regex does not prove which pattern matched; when paired, the issued regex is the pattern. The 22-result, 5:43 1-result, 5:48 12-result, 5:54 6-result, and 6:08 8-result headers are each not paired with an issued regex in the batch that returned them, so those patterns are unknown and must not be invented. The 6:04 “Found 0 results” header names no path, regex, or file pattern and is not paired in that batch with an issued search, so it must not be assigned to any earlier unreturned search and its pattern must not be invented. The 6:08 “Found 8 results” header also names no regex or file pattern and is not paired in that batch with an issued search. It must not be assigned to the 11:35:49 search, the 11:38:40 App.tsx search, the 5:32:45 taskService search, the 5:56 treeService search, the 5:59 `src` search, the 6:02 unexecuted search, the 6:04 HomeScreen search, or the 6:15/6:20 supabase search. It is distinct from the earlier 11:35:49 “Found 8 results” printout, which quoted HomeScreen lines 13–15 and 227–229 and mentioned `@treeapp/notices-v1` in appDialog; the 6:08 groups are only the migration file. The 6:20 “Found 11 results” header also does not restate a regex, but it is the return of the search issued at 6:15 (`INSERT INTO|tree_id|CREATE TRIGGER|tasks`, `*.sql` on `supabase`). It is distinct from the 6:08 8-result search and from the 11:35:49 8-result printout. Its groups are only `001_add_tree_columns.sql`. The 6:06 treeStore result is a file read, not a search. The 6:09 types result is a file read, not a search, and is not the TreeDetailScreen read. The 6:11 TreeDetailScreen result is a file read, not a search, and must not be assigned to the SQL search or to any earlier unpaired search. Printed search groups are hit context only. Zero groups means no file text. A command result that omits the command string does not by itself prove which command ran; when paired, record both and still treat empty exit-0 stdout as reported success and no captured stdout only. Exit 0 with a listing or JSON confirms that printed listing or JSON only. Exit 1 whose stdout is a shell “not recognized” message confirms that failure text only. “Successfully deleted” one path confirms deletion of that path only. An `apply_patch` / `edit` / `write_to_file` body is intended text until a result says otherwise. When the result says `modified` with no diff, the path was modified and the body remains intended text, not a proven hunk and not a confirmed prior read. If the issued edit body is not in the batch that returns the no-diff result, do not invent the intended old or new text; the 2:25:58 body was already recorded from that earlier batch and stays intended text. Assistant prose is intent only. An environment reminder list is not a build log and not an `update_todo_list` result. The 2:25:18, 2:25:58, and 2:27:15 “You have not created a todo list yet” lines are reminder displays only. Reminder tables: 5:32:45 through 6:11:57 showed three planted-tree card items, all Completed; 6:15:09 showed item 1 In Progress and items 2 and 3 Pending; 6:20:30 shows items 1 and 2 In Progress and item 3 Pending. All are reminder displays only, not an `update_todo_list` result, not a source change, and not acceptance. The 6:20 display is the later reminder text; it does not prove a todo write. A visible-file, open-tab, or workspace-file line is not a read. A “You did not use a tool” error is automation, not a write. The 5:56, 5:59, 6:02, 6:04, 6:06, 6:08, 6:09, and 6:11 “You did not use a tool in your previous response” errors are that automation, as are two further ones after the SQL search result and by 6:20:30. A tool-result error that a `search_files` was not executed because a tool was already used in that message confirms only that the search did not run. The 6:04 and 6:08 interruption notices that only one tool may be used at a time are not search or read results. The 6:11 batch has no such interruption on the TreeDetailScreen read. The 6:20 SQL result is a completed search, not an interruption. A printed `ok` / `MISSING` line is that probe’s label, not a migration and not a full schema. A printed row count or delete JSON from an anon client confirms only what that invocation printed. A later sample-count JSON supersedes the live count for those named tables only as of that later invocation. A `select('*')` limited to 3 rows confirms the printed count, error field, and mapped sample fields only. Code that selects or writes a column is not proof the live column exists. A migration file’s `ALTER TABLE` / `CREATE INDEX` / `UPDATE` / `SELECT count(*)` / policy / constraint text is file text of the printed lines only, not proof the migration ran, not a live schema, and not a count result. A TypeScript interface field is file text of the printed lines only, not proof a live column exists and not proof a screen maps that field. A user’s claim is not a deletion, not a new probe, and not an image read. An image mentioned without a described image body is not an image read. A later confirmed read shows file text of the cited lines as of that read; a later no-diff write of the same path means those lines are no longer proven current. The 6:11 TreeDetailScreen read is after the 2:27:15 no-diff write, so lines 250–319 are file text as of that read; it does not make lines 1057–1091 current and does not reveal either no-diff hunk. A function doc comment or nearby comment is file text at the printed lines, not proof the described fallback runs. An edit `old_string` is intended prior text, not a confirmed read, except where the same characters were already printed by a paired read. A select-count command is not a delete. A node script that `readFileSync`s `src/services/supabase.ts` and regex-extracts URL and anon key does not print that file. A content-wrapper attribute that claims a line range does not invent lines that are not printed. The 6:06 treeStore wrapper said `lines="1-80"` but the numbered body stops at line 27; lines 28–80 must not be invented. The 6:08 search prints eight windows of the migration file and does not print lines between those windows. The 6:20 search prints eleven windows and does not print lines between those windows. The 6:09 types wrapper said `lines="90-159"` and the numbered body is printed through line 159; lines before 90 and after 159 must not be invented. Line 159 is only the opening of `RootStackParamList`; its members are not printed. The 6:11 TreeDetailScreen wrapper said `lines="250-319"` and the numbered body is printed through line 319; lines before 250 and after 319 must not be invented from that read. None of the items below is user-accepted.

The 11:35:49 “Found 8 results” printout is not a write, not a deletion, and not a schema probe, and it is not the 6:08 “Found 8 results” and not the 6:20 “Found 11 results.” The 11:35:49 issued search still has no result at 6:20. The 11:38:40 issued App.tsx search still has no result; the App.tsx lines 1–30 tool result is a file read, not that search. The 12:10:31 HomeScreen read is lines 290–344 only. The 12:22:33 TaskScreen search is a different returned search. The 2:25:58 TreeDetailScreen read quotes lines 1057–1091 only. Issued parameters were offset 1080 limit 100; the printed window is 1057–1091, so lines before 1057 and after 1091 were unread by that read, and a 100-line span from 1080 was not returned. It predates the 2:27:15 no-diff write, so it is not current source after that write. The 6:11 read of 250–319 does not reprint 154–156, 589–591, or 1057–1091 and does not fill that gap. The pre-5:37 22-result search prints History TreeDetailScreen lines 589–591 only. The 5:43 and 5:48 searches do not reprint TreeDetailScreen. The 5:54 search prints TreeDetailScreen 154–156 only. The 5:56 HistoryScreen read, the 5:59 and 6:02 treeService reads, the 6:04 0-result search, the 6:06 treeStore read, the 6:08 SQL search, the 6:09 types read, the 6:11 TreeDetailScreen read, and the 6:20 SQL search do not reprint each other’s non-overlapping files. The 6:20 search does not reprint TreeDetailScreen.

Prior stored memory was cut mid-item more than once (storage truncation, not new tool results), including cutoffs at “update_todo_list re”, the 12:22:33 TaskScreen search, “The 2:25:58 read of lines 1”, “the photo and loca”, the 5:48 issued treeService read parameters, the 5:54 treeService hit (“Body after `id: s”), the 5:48 HistoryScreen hit at `if (tasksRes.data) setTasks(`, “do not print `ca`, and the 6:08 migration window at `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tree_moni`. The 2:25:58 read is lines 1057–1091, not a read of line 1. The 5:48 issued read parameters remain offset 469, limit 80, slice, anchor_line 470, max_levels 1, include_siblings false, include_header false, max_lines 80; that read still has no result at 6:20. The 5:43 hit is only the comment, `export async function fetchTreeById(`, and `id: string`; the function body is not printed. The exact 12:02:49 delete JSON payload is not restated and must not be invented; the paired result was exit code 0 and a printed delete JSON for that `tree_records` delete invocation only. The 12:06:23 completion body after “before com” is not restated and must not be invented. The 12:09:16 sample-count JSON body is not fully restated; this anon client still saw 1 `tree_records` row and 16 `projects` rows at that invocation. The 11:58:09 count JSON is truncated after `"trees":97,"treesE`; do not invent the rest. Do not invent the 2:25:18 TreeDetailScreen hunk. Do not invent TreeDetailScreen lines outside the printed windows (250–319 as of the 6:11 read; 1057–1091 as of the 2:25:58 read, not proven current after 2:27:15; 589–591 and 154–156 as search context only). Do not treat either the 2:25:58 intended edit or the 2:27:15 intended edit as current source. Do not treat the 2:27:15 edit `old_string` as a confirmed read. Do not invent a taskService.ts search result or file body. Do not invent the regex of the 22-result, 5:43, 5:48, 5:54, 6:04, or 6:08 searches. Do not invent a result for the 5:56 treeService search, the 5:59 `src` search, the 6:02 unexecuted search, the 6:02 HomeScreen read, the 6:04 HomeScreen search, the 6:06 TaskScreen read, or the 6:08 TaskScreen read. The 6:15 supabase search now has a result; do not invent SQL outside its eleven printed windows, and do not invent the 6:08 windows’ unread text from the old `tree_moni` cutoff. Do not invent the parameters of the 6:02 search that was not executed. Do not invent types/index.ts lines outside 90–159. Do not invent treeService.ts lines outside the 11:15 read (220–299), the 5:59 read (310–449), the 6:02 printed read (680–796), the 5:43 / 5:54 hit (469–471), and the 5:48 hits (18–20 and 66–68). Lines 300–309, 450–468, and 472–679 are unread. Lines 797+ are unread; the 6:02 wrapper said `680-799` but the printed body stops at 796. The 469–471 hit stops at `id: string`. The 5:48 `insertTreeRecord` hit stops at `record: TreeRecordInsert`. The 5:48 lines 18–20 are a comment only. Do not invent treeStore.ts lines outside 1–27. HistoryScreen confirmed text is the 5:48 hit windows (125–127 and 133–135, hit context only; 125–127 was storage-truncated at `if (tasksRes.data) setTasks(`) plus the 5:56 read of lines 340–419. Lines 340–419 do not supersede 125–127 or 133–135. Results from 5:59 through 6:20 do not print HistoryScreen. The 6:06 treeStore read shows `setTrees` and `addTree` in `treeStore.ts` only; it does not print `postgres_changes`. The 6:08 and 6:20 printed SQL windows do not contain `postgres_changes`, `setTrees`, `addTree`, `TreeCard`, `completedItems`, `Saag`, or `renderTask`. The 6:09 types window contains `setTasks` and `setActiveTaskId` on `TaskState`, not `setTrees` or `addTree`. The 6:11 TreeDetailScreen window contains `tree.id`, `tree.latitude` / `task?.latitude`, `tree.longitude` / `task?.longitude`, `displayTreeId(tree)`, `parseTreeMeta(tree.notes)`, `tree.scientific_name`, and `tree.dbh_cm`; it does not print `postgres_changes`, `setTrees`, `addTree`, `TreeCard`, `completedItems`, `Saag`, `renderTask`, or a photo field. Do not treat assistant IDs `E9AE1C18` and `TREE-A38IN14` as file text; they are not in the printed hits, including TreeDetailScreen 250–319 and the SQL windows, and the 6:04 result printed no groups. The 5:59 assistant sentence that those two ids are the same tree, one with photo and location and one without, is prose only.

## Relevant Files & Code
Confirmed no-diff modifications (path only, hunk not proven): 2:15 App.tsx; several EditTreeScreen.tsx notices through 4:33; TaskScreen.tsx (pre-2:24, 2:55, 4:35:28 PM, 8:14, 8:18, and 12:16:25 PM); non-History `src/screens/TreeDetailScreen.tsx` (before-2:30, 3:34); 3:24 auditService.ts; 12:58:39 PM `src/services/treeLocationService.js`; 1:32:48 PM `src/screens/Map/TreeMapScreen.tsx`; 4:45:10 PM `src/screens/History/UpdateTreeScreen.tsx`; 6:17:48 PM `src/services/treeService.ts`; 6:25:31 PM History `TreeDetailScreen.tsx`; 10/5 11:13 AM `treeService.ts`; 11:33:37 AM `HomeScreen.tsx`; 11:35:06 AM `ProjectSelectScreen.tsx`; 11:40:19 AM `authStore.ts`; 11:42:29 AM `appDialog.tsx`; 12:16:25 PM `TaskScreen.tsx` (`modified`, no diff, baseline notice, no TypeScript problems, no quoted lines); 2:25:18 PM History `TreeDetailScreen.tsx` (same); 2:27:15 PM History `TreeDetailScreen.tsx` again (`modified`, no diff, “seen all changes / new baseline,” no TS problems, no quoted lines). The 2:27:15 result is the return of the edit issued at 2:25:58. It is a later no-diff modification of the same History path already modified with no diff at 6:25:31 PM and 2:25:18 PM. It does not show whether the bytes differ from either earlier result and does not reveal any hunk. The 2:25:58 read of lines 1057–1091 is earlier than this write. The 2:27:15 issued edit (Post-Audit / `auditStatus.currentRound`) has no result through 6:20 and is not another no-diff modification. No new `file_write_result` from 5:32:45 through 6:20:30. The 6:11 TreeDetailScreen read of 250–319 is later file text of a different window, not a hunk of those writes, and does not show Post-Audit or `auditStatus.currentRound`. The 5:43/5:54 hits at 469–471, the 5:48 hits at 18–20 and 66–68, the 5:59 lines 310–449, and the 6:02 lines 680–796 do not reveal the 6:17:48 or 11:13 treeService hunks. The 5:54 call-site windows do not reveal earlier no-diff hunks. HistoryScreen 340–419 is not a write. TreeCard.tsx being visible or tabbed is not a write. Opening `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG` is not a write and not a read. The 6:06 treeStore read, the 6:08 migration search, the 6:09 types read, the 6:11 TreeDetailScreen read, and the 6:20 SQL search are not writes and not proof any SQL ran.
